sections.churn_summary: Hold-buffer guards are aligned on the three focus tracks (`exit_confirm_screens=2`, `reentry_cooldown_screens=1`, `min_rebalance_notional_gbp=10.0`), and the last 7-day operational window looks stable: each focus track shows `duplicate_day_skip=false`, `adjacent_flip_count=0`, and the latest pass executed zero trades with `buffer_holds_planned=0` and `reentry_skips_planned=0`. Lifetime decision-review cost drag is still high on control and primary (`rules` 0.4163 / 69 trades; `ai_judgment` 0.3524 / 51 trades), with watch alerts, though epoch-scoped drag on primary is lower than control (`learning_tracks_review.reviews.ai_judgment.metrics.epoch.cost_drag` 0.1491 vs `rules` 0.2566). The 7-day buffered-hold replay still favours two confirmation screens: lowering to one screen adds 9 trades and +11.73pp simulated cost drag on `rules` and 8 trades and +12.36pp on `ai_judgment` (`buffered_hold_counterfactual.summary`). The largest operational learning gap is the exit-shadow cohort: `closed_count=0` on all focus tracks (`exit_shadow`), so grace-vs-rotation learning cannot start despite active `exit_streak` on KLR.L and `buffered_holdings=1` on `rules` and `ai_judgment`.
